subject: Unexpected September overage & VAT handling for MerchantCo account
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@merchantco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice 202509 - unexpected spike and VAT question

Hi Jonas,

We received invoice 202509 this morning and there is a ~3.2x usage jump compared to August. The line item shows a large number of "ingest" tokens originating from the EU region and the VAT on the invoice doubled as a result. We've attached the invoice and a small sample of the usage rows where this spike appears.

Can you confirm:
- What caused the sudden token increase (any known deploys or changes on your side)?
- Whether these tokens are billable (some look like staging/test pushes) and if we should expect a credit?
- How Redwood intends to handle the VAT for any adjustment (reverse-charge vs. grossed-up credit) — our finance team requires the VAT flow documented.

We need this clarified before our AP team releases payment. If helpful, please put a temporary hold on collection while we investigate.

Attachments: invoice_202509.pdf (1 page), usage_sample.csv (100 rows)

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Finance, MerchantCo
lena.ortiz@merchantco.com
+44 20 7100 4455

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@merchantco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 202509 - unexpected spike and VAT question

Hi Lena — thanks for the heads up and the sample. Sorry for the disruption. I'm looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (billing/finance) to help triage and confirm whether those tokens were from production or test/staging.

Immediate next steps:
- Ben: can you pull the detailed usage export for MerchantCo for the last 30 days and sanity-check for any ingestion anomalies?
- Laura: if we confirm a customer-side staging leak or mis-tagged environment, can Redwood issue a one-time pro-rata credit and describe the VAT handling options?

Lena — we'll aim to get preliminary findings within 24 hours. If a temporary collection hold makes internal sense, we'll mark the invoice Pending in our billing console until we resolve.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 202509 - unexpected spike and VAT question

Quick update from my side after a first-pass on telemetry:
- There's a burst of rapid short-lived sessions tagged "merchantco-ingest" between 2025-09-27 02:10:00Z and 2025-09-28 04:40:00Z.
- The token distribution indicates many small requests (high request count, low tokens/request) consistent with a bulk upload job rather than normal app traffic.
- Possible causes: customer-side test runner hitting production keys, or an accidental replay job from their ETL.

I'm requesting a full usage export (per-request) from platform logs and will attach the CSV when ready. I also raised internal ops ticket RG-UST-412 to correlate keys to environment tags — that should tell us whether the API key used was bound to a staging project.

Attachment: export-request-ticket-RG-UST-412.pdf

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@merchantco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-05T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice 202509 - unexpected spike and VAT question

Hi Lena — thanks for waiting. Attaching the short excerpt of the per-request export and a trimmed token trace that shows the burst window. Highlights:
- The majority of the spike maps to API key ending in "-mco-prod" but environment metadata is inconsistent on a subset of requests.
- We found ~28k requests that were tagged with a blank environment label; many of those came from two IP ranges that belong to your CDN vendor.

Preliminary recommendation: we can issue a one-time adjustment credit for the subset we reasonably classify as "non-customer production" (test/replay) — estimated credit: 62,300 tokens (net $125.40). For VAT: because MerchantCo is an EU-registered entity and the usage occurred in EU-region capacity, we propose issuing the credit net of VAT and documenting the reverse-charge on your side. That means Redwood will reduce the invoice amount and provide a new invoice/credit memo showing the netted VAT treatment.

Attachments: token-sample-20250930.csv (excerpt), usage_trace.log (trimmed)

Jonas
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-10-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice 202509 adjustment and VAT confirmation

Hi Lena — thanks for the details. We've reviewed the excerpts Jonas provided and validated against the ledger. Finance can issue a one-time credit memo for the amount Jonas quoted (net $125.40) and reissue the corrected invoice for September.

VAT handling: because MerchantCo provided a valid EU VAT number (please confirm below) and is registered in the EU, Redwood will treat the adjustment as a net (reverse-charge) correction. The credit memo and reissued invoice will show the net amounts and reference the reverse-charge tax code. Our billing system will:
- Mark the original invoice 202509 as Adjusted
- Publish credit memo CM-20251006-777 which offsets the net amount
- Reissue invoice 202509-R with the corrected net and VAT references

Next steps for you: please reply with your company VAT number and confirm you accept the reverse-charge approach. Once we have confirmation we'll:
- Apply the credit (visible in your billing console within 2 business days)
- Reissue the adjusted invoice and send both documents to your AP team

Related links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Laura — confirmed. MerchantCo VAT: GB123456789. We accept the reverse-charge correction and the proposed credit.

Please confirm:
- When the credit will appear in our account (you mentioned 2 business days)
- Whether Redwood will send the reissued invoice directly to our AP inbox (finance@merchantco.com) and mark the original invoice as "do not pay" in the portal

Once we see the credit and the corrected invoice we'll release payment for the remaining balance. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Finance, MerchantCo
